messages:
alex: Heads-up — we started getting customer-reported p95 spikes on text-gen routes at ~03:10 UTC. Baseline 180ms -> p95 ~950ms, p99 ~1.6s. No deploys at the time.
maria: Seen the alerts, investigating. Grafana shows a sudden increase in KV cache miss rate for serving-shard-7. Miss rate jumped from 4% -> 42% around 03:08.
sam: @maria can you dump recent cache metrics and a small sample of keys? suspect warmup fallout after the maintenance window.
maria: Attaching quick snippet from metrics (truncated):
```
metric: kv_prefix_miss_rate{shard="7"} 0.42
metric: kv_prefix_evictions_per_min 198
metric: req_latency_p95 0.95
hot_keys_count 123
```
jamie: Interesting — evictions spiked too. Could be a policy regression that changed target size or TTL. Any config pushes to prefix-evict?
alex: No config pushes recorded. Ops-bot: autoscaler executed routine node recycle at 02:58 UTC in region us-west-2, replaced 2/64 nodes in serving pool.
sam: Node recycles could blow away in-memory warm cache and trigger heavy warmup if many unique prefix keys stream through. But miss rate is unusually high for warmup traffic; looks like keys are more diverse.
maria: I pulled a few example keys from logs around 03:09: 
```
customer:acct:prod:acct_7a9f:session_0b3f
customer:acct:prod:acct_7a9f:session_84aa
legacy-header|acct_7a9f|nlp_version=2
X-User-Session:acct_7a9f:ctx
```
jamie: Those header-derived keys are noisy. We normalize headers into prefix keys but there was a recent change in request tagging that appends a region tag to the header on some clients. That would inflate cardinality.
sam: That matches the sudden entropy increase. Miss rate x10 + evictions -> p95. Two potential mitigations: 1) temporarily increase cache capacity on serving-shard-7 or 2) enable a stricter prefix normalization to collapse header variants. Which is faster?
alex: Short-term: bump in-memory cache allocation and raise max_items for shard-7. Medium: roll a hotfix to normalization mapping to strip region suffix for now.
maria: I'll run a one-off scale-up via infra tooling. Command: `infractl scale runtime-shard --id=7 --delta=+2` — applying now.
ops-bot: infractl: scale job accepted (job id: 8a7f). New allocation expected in ~90s.
jamie: While that's rolling, we can also patch eviction policy to favor sticky prefixes (sessions) with a small TTL bias. Patch is trivial but needs canary.
sam: Can we add a fast filter to drop header-derived keys above pattern `^legacy-header\|` from being emitted to KV? Quick config change at the routing stage could prevent new noisy keys.
maria: Deployed a routing filter to sandbox tier to test; rolling to prod in 2m if no errors.
alex: After infra bump and filter, p95 moved down to 230ms within ~4min. Miss rate dropped to ~6%.
maria: Confirming: kv_prefix_miss_rate now 0.06 on shard-7. Evictions back to normal.
jamie: Followups: 1) create a regression test that simulates header-variant explosion and measures miss/evict. 2) Add metric for prefix-cardinality-change to detect sudden entropy shifts. 3) Revisit normalization rules and formalize header-to-prefix mapping.
sam: Also add alert runbook: if shard miss rate increases >15% AND evictions >100/min, auto-scale + routing filter toggle. Saves paging for ops.
alex: I'll file the postmortem and link configs. Quick repro steps (for the eng-runtime playbook):
```
1) simulate traffic with header variants: for i in {1..10000}; do curl -H "X-Client-Tag: region-$((i%50))" https://serving.example/api/gen; done
2) tail kv metrics: kubectl logs -l app=kv-cache -c metrics
3) observe miss_rate, evictions, and p95
```
maria: Documented the incident in ops notes, saving relevant graphs. I'm keeping the filter live but we'll refine mapping next week.
ops-bot: Incident resolved flagged.
alex: Thanks all. No customer-facing action required; we notified support and closed the escalations. We'll follow up with a small RFC for normalization + the new cardinality metric. :thumbsup:
